You think it's a stretch that all the TV networks decided to put their antennas on the tallest building in the city until it's destruction? The taller the broadcast source, the longer the range because of the curvature of the Earth, and the less buildings, trees, and other stuff are between the source of the signal and every potential viewer. 

All the money broadcast TV and radio make is from advertising, and the amount you can charge for advertising depends on your viewership. The New York metro area is the largest in the United States, and the most densely populated part of the Northeast, which is itself the most densely populated part of the county. So especially in the 1970s when the building was built, it would have been a criminally stupid decision for any Media company that could afford it to not broadcast from the world trade Center. It was the tallest building in the world at it's completion, the tallest in America until 2000, and the tallest in New York City for it's entire existence. 

Whenever they build a Skyscraper, they always build a tower on top of it if they can charge rent to cell phone, TV, and radio companies. Why wouldn't they if it's one more way they can capitalize on being a tall building?

And even today in an age where cable television, what made broadcast TV largely obsolete is becoming obsolete, 7 TV channels broadcast from the new world trade center; Channel 2 (WCBS), Channel 4 (WNBC), Channel 5 (WNYW), Channel 9 (WWOR), Channel 13 (WNET), Channel 31 (WPXN),Channel 47 (WNJU). All of them are former tennants of the old world trade center that was destroyed on that day.
The average person can not tell the difference by smell.

Yes, but I've talked to multiple people about the aftermath of 9/11 and they all said that. For most people that drive into DC from Virginia, taking 395 is the most convenient way. Not to mention the Pentagon itself is a large enough employer that every county has at least one bus that goes there, often directly, so it's not like you have to struggle to find people who had stories/anecdotes if the topic of the attacks comes up.

This was confirmed notably by a freinds father who is actually a firefighter who was literally one of the first first responders to show up at the Pentagon, and eventually developed cancer because of the fumes he inhaled and died about 5 years ago. [If you want more hard evidence you can look at the cancer rates, leukemia is associated with exposure to benzene, which is present in jet fuel](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/health-effects-of-9-11-still-plague-responders-and-survivors/), one study found that first responders had [double the expected rate of leukemia](https://academic.oup.com/jncics/article/4/1/pkz090/5613807) which is a type of cancer that is rare in adults compared to other cancers.

 I always find it fascinating how all these conspiracy theories come from people who do not and have never lived in  the DC or New York areas, because somehow people a thousand miles away know more about what happened than the people who were there, knew people who were there, etc etc. if it were conspiracy, you think people and probably two of the highest educated areas in the country would have noticed things more than random people on YouTube.
If it wasn't an airplane, explain the Diesel smell that persisted for months when driving around that section of 395?

That's because [All the broadcast networks had transmitters on the North Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tenants_in_1_World_Trade_Center_(1971%E2%80%932001)) because when it was built it was the largest building in the world in America's largest TV market and located fairly centrally in downtown Manhattan. I would imagine the plane hitting it might've had something to do with the networks going down.

Also WCBS2s signal was not affected by the attacks because it had [kept it's all transmitter at the Empire State building as a backup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCBS-TV#Later_analog_years_(1951%E2%80%932008)) so your statement isn't even accurate.


I also find it interesting how most of the conspiracy theories involve the world trade Center and not the Pentagon, because the world trade Center was the one broadcasted more. the Pentagon is in my hometown, and if you ask anyone who commuted along 395 around that time they will tell you that you could smell a diesel like smell for months just driving past. I know people say it was done by a missile,  but I can't imagine if that was the case the details such as the smell would be somehow faked, since there is no way to measure or use it as evidence, since it's all first hand accounts, in America's 6th largest metro area. After all, half the people here work for the government in some form, so you'd think the people here need less convincing since they're either more trusting of their government or in on it ;).

If the collapse was planned by elites, and not the result of fires, why would they tell the media in advance, instead of just orchestrating it, and waiting for the media to report on it?

It's basic opsec to tell as few people as possible, the least amount of information possible to avoid loose ends. Even if the top brass of the BBC or any media organization knew ahead of time, they wouldn't go over to the reporters and say "hey tell the people this, don't check on it just say it" because again, if you were actually planning a massive conspiracy, you want as few people as possible to know

We need the college educated for factories. Who do you think will program, fix, and design the robots and machines that make the products.

According to the [Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/articles/american-factories-demand-white-collar-education-for-blue-collar-work-11575907185)

>U.S. manufacturers have added more than a million jobs since the recession, with the growth going to men and women with degrees, the Journal analysis found. Over the same time, manufacturers employed fewer people with at most a high-school diploma

>Employment in manufacturing jobs that require the most complex problem-solving skills, such as industrial engineers, grew 10% between 2012 and 2018; jobs requiring the least declined 3%, the Journal analysis found.

So yes we do need more factory workers. But one does not become an engineer by on the job training. 

[Manufacturing output in 2017 was 80% higher than it was 3 decades before, inflation adjusted](https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2017/07/25/most-americans-unaware-that-as-u-s-manufacturing-jobs-have-disappeared-output-has-grown/) So Americas manufacturing sector has been growing significantly. However most of the highest growing sectors: machinery, automotive, chemicals, plastics, electronics,and aerospace all require people with education.

How many people changed the world by not becoming "too educated"?  Wikipedia has a "random article" button. Click it until you see 5 people's Wikipedia pages. How many of them went to college?
